To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the As atoms are incorporated in the bulk of Al(1-x )Ga(x)As oxide and that the oxide/GaAs interface is abrupt and that the interface strain is compressive.
the As is incorporated into the interface layer in the form of As2 and As4 and that the interface is strained.

(1) GaAs substrate and Al(1-x )Ga(x)As oxide film are bonded through the As-O bond at the interface; (2) the As atoms are not incorporated into the oxide layer, but are bonded to the Ga atoms in the substrate; (3) the oxide is amorphous and the density of the oxide film is about 2.5 g/cm(3) which is about 30% lower than that of the bulk oxide.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the local structure of the interface between III-V compound semiconductor native oxides (Al2O3, Al2O3/Ga2O3) and GaAs substrate, and with the local structure at the interface between III-N compound native oxides and GaAs.
the structural and electronic characterization of the native oxides on III-V compound semiconductor surfaces and the interface between the oxide film and GaAs.
the local structural characterization of the native oxide/Ga(As) interface by using XAFS.

the interface between the native oxide Al(1- x)Ga(x) As and GaAs substrate is a complex one and that the interfacial region contains a number of different As species, which are not present in the bulk oxide.
the Ga-As bond is broken at the interface and the As is incorporated in the oxide as AsO4 tetrahedra.
the As atoms are incorporated into the interface region, but not in the bulk oxide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interface is very smooth with a density profile that is consistent with an abrupt transition.
the As is incorporated in a form of As2O5 at the interface, and that the interfacial oxide is under tensile strain.
the GaAs substrate is oxidized by the AlGaAs film, and that the As is incorporated in the oxide film at the interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the As is incorporated into the Al(1-x)(Ga(x)As) native oxide and that the As is in the form of As2O3 at the interface with GaAs.
the GaAs substrate and Al(1-x )Ga(x)As oxide layer have different density profiles.
As atoms are present at the interface, and that the As atoms have a local environment similar to that in GaAs.
